def test_format_int_list__mixed_singles_and_ranges():
    # Mix of singletons and contiguous ranges.
    input_list = [1, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 15]
    result = format_int_list(input_list)
    assert result == "1,3,5-8,10-11,15"


def test_args2cmd__args_with_double_quotes():

    assert args2cmd(['dd"dd']) == 'dd\\"dd'


def test_singularize__default_strip_s():
    # Words ending with a single 's' that are not caught by earlier rules
    assert singularize("cats") == "cat"
    assert singularize("Cats") == "Cat"
    assert singularize("CATS") == "CAT"

def test_asciify__non_ascii_str_ignore_true_drops():

def test_ellipsize__cut_at_space_strip_punctuation():
    # From the library docstring
    text = "Beautiful is better than ugly. Explicit is better."
    # limit = 31, ellipsis length = 1, so cut should happen before the period
    expected = "Beautiful is better than ugly…"
    result = ellipsize(text, max_len=31)
    assert result == expected

# ---------- error handling ----------
def test_ellipsize__max_len_not_greater_than_ellipsis():
    # default ellipsis length is 1, so max_len == 1 should raise
    with pytest.raises(ValueError) as excinfo:
        ellipsize("any text", max_len=1)
    assert "expected max_len greater than length of" in str(excinfo.value)

    # custom longer ellipsis
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        ellipsize("any", max_len=2, ellipsis="...")

def test_pluralize__irregular_singular():
    # Pick a known irregular singular from the map
    singular = next(iter(_IRR_S2P))
    expected = _IRR_S2P[singular]

    # lower‑case
    assert pluralize(singular) == expected
    # title‑case preservation
    assert pluralize(singular.title()) == expected.title()
    # upper‑case preservation
    assert pluralize(singular.upper()) == expected.upper()

def test_ordinalize__ext_only_flag():
    """Edge case: ext_only flag returns only the suffix."""
    # Basic single-digit suffixes
    assert ordinalize(1, ext_only=True) == "st"
    assert ordinalize(2, ext_only=True) == "nd"
    assert ordinalize(3, ext_only=True) == "rd"
    # A typical non‑teen, non‑1/2/3 case
    assert ordinalize(4, ext_only=True) == "th"
    # Teen numbers (should all be 'th')
    assert ordinalize(11, ext_only=True) == "th"
    assert ordinalize(12, ext_only=True) == "th"
    assert ordinalize(13, ext_only=True) == "th"
    # Numbers past the teen range to verify normal rules resume
    assert ordinalize(21, ext_only=True) == "st"
    assert ordinalize(22, ext_only=True) == "nd"
    assert ordinalize(23, ext_only=True) == "rd"
    assert ordinalize(24, ext_only=True) == "th"

def _new_extractor():
    """Helper to create a fresh HTMLTextExtractor with a known empty result list."""
    extractor = HTMLTextExtractor()
    # Ensure the extractor has a `result` attribute that is a list.
    # The implementation of HTMLTextExtractor in boltons creates this attribute,
    # but we guard against accidental changes.
    if not hasattr(extractor, "result"):
        extractor.result = []
    return extractor


def test_HTMLTextExtractor_handle_charref__hex_uppercase_charref():

def _is_gzip(data: bytes) -> bool:
    """Return True if data starts with the gzip magic header."""
    return data[:2] == b"\x1f\x8b"


def test_gzip_bytes__empty_bytes():
    """Empty input bytes should produce a valid gzip payload that decompresses to empty."""
    result = gzip_bytes(b"")
    # The result must be bytes and start with the gzip header.
    assert isinstance(result, bytes)
    assert _is_gzip(result)
    # Decompressing should give back an empty bytes object.
    assert gzip.decompress(result) == b""
